utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Good to see you. How's the week been?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Brutal honestly. My manager is absolutely insufferable. She micromanages everything and second-guesses every decision I make. I spent twenty hours on a report and she sent it back for revisions over one typo.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: That sounds incredibly frustrating. How does working under that kind of scrutiny affect your confidence?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: It makes me second-guess myself constantly. I used to love this job but now I dread going in. I've started updating my resume. I think it's time to leave. She's going to regret losing me when she sees the numbers tank without me.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Recognizing when a work environment is toxic is a form of self-advocacy. What's holding you back from making the move?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Fear mostly. My mortgage. But I've been saving. I also have an interview next week at a startup. I'm not going to waste my potential in this job anymore. I need to make them regret not promoting me sooner.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: That forward-thinking is healthy. How are things outside of work? You mentioned your partner last session.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Much better actually. We had a great weekend. Went hiking. My partner is being really supportive through all of this. I'm frustrated with work but I'm genuinely okay overall. Just venting today, I think.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Venting is valid and useful. Sometimes naming the frustration is the first step. Let's use the rest of our time to think through your exit plan.
